mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the decision date is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financing conditions affecting corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: Over a 5-year window, no significant negative 20d returns after such rate spikes when inflation is controlled (< 2%).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) followed by a subsequent decline predict a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market interprets improving labor market conditions.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS shows a double bottom pattern (increase then decrease) over the next 3 months
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive returns over 60 days when the double bottom is not confirmed by subsequent employment data.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% is followed by a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals weakening manufacturing demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 10 such events, less than 30% produce negative 20d returns, or INDPRO recovers within 4 months without a follow-on return drag.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% for three consecutive months is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as expectations for future rate cuts improve.
failure_condition: No positive 20d returns when CPIAUCSL recovers rapidly or inflation spikes unexpectedly within 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month moving average of the S&P 500 home trade volume (HOUST) exceeds 1.5 standard deviations above its mean, the next 5-day S&P 500 forward return is positive, reflecting short-term demand surges.
failure_condition: No significant return advantage in non-financial crisis periods or when volume spike is not confirmed by order book data.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a decline in monthly pay growth (implied by industrial production and wage data) predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 returns as labor market weakness persists.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases while INDPRO declines over the next 3 months
failure_condition: No consistent negative returns when pay growth (e.g., wage index) also rises or UNRATE falls instead.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in retail sales (implied by PAYEMS or broader demand proxies not available) followed by a rebound within 20 days predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates a bottom in consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS shows a 'rebound' after a >10% monthly decline
failure_condition: No positive returns if rebound is not confirmed by subsequent sales data or if broader retail activity does not improve.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of real GDP growth (not directly observable but proxyable via INDPRO and external estimates at decision date) turns negative, the 60-day S&P 500 forward return is negative, reflecting supply-side constraints.
failure_condition: No negative returns when GDP growth is estimated positive or when supply constraints are not confirmed by other indicators (e.g., capacity utilization).
